payload.text:
Radial-velocity dataset seed96_diff3.

- 75 observations over a baseline of 106.7 days
- median reported uncertainty: 1.05 m/s
- instruments: instA
- host star mass: 1.14 solar masses
- submission attempts available: 5

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Initial hypothesis: start with a 1-planet model at 31.38 days.

Why:
- The strongest peak at 106.7 d is essentially the observing baseline itself (106.65 d), so it is not a constrained planetary period.
- The 31.38 d peak is the strongest non-baseline candidate, with very low approximate FAP (~1.8e-5), low spectral-window power there, and it is not an obvious 1-day cadence artifact.
- The shorter-period peaks near 0.52–1.2 d are weak, high-FAP, and several sit near cadence/window structure or plausible aliases, so they are not good first-planet choices.

So the simplest supported model is:
- Planet b: P ≈ 31.38 d

Please fit that first. After fitting, inspect residuals to see whether any surviving signal is real or just aliases/harmonics.

HANDOFF: engineer
